methods.name: Morse code read as a binary number
methods.summary: Spell a word in International Morse, write dah as 1 and dit as 0, run the letters together and read the bit string as a base-two integer. Penn calls this the 'mainstay of Zodiacese'.
methods.rules: Use International Morse with dit = 0 and dah = 1 (A=01 B=1000 C=1010 D=100 E=0 F=0010 G=110 H=0000 I=00 J=0111 K=101 L=0100 M=11 N=10 O=111 P=0110 Q=1101 R=010 S=000 T=1 U=001 V=0001 W=011 X=1001 Y=1011 Z=1100). Drop letter boundaries and spaces, and read the concatenation as a base-two number. Leading zeros do not count. Arabic numerals inside a phrase are written as plain binary, not Morse digits (TIMES 17 -> 1 00 11 0 000 10001). The resulting number is the word's 'digital spelling'. Penn's reference chart 'Writing Digitally' (T17 p.18; SP front matter) lists the letter table, the Morse digits and binary 1-100. Variant (Polarity swap (dash = 0, dot = 1)): In a 1981 interview Penn said the Zodiac sometimes substituted 'dashes for ones, dots for zeros, and vice versa'. The default is dah = 1, dit = 0. Penn's 1981 description allows the opposite assignment as well. Later sources use only dah = 1. Example: Binary Morse ('Oakes' in Laube 1981) -> 'substituting dashes for ones, dots for zeros, and vice versa' (No worked example given; later works never invert.)

methods.name: Leading zeros vanish (dit-initial words are inexpressible)
methods.summary: A bit string's leading zeros do not count, so a word that starts with a dit loses those bits. Penn uses this to explain word order and why some codes are 'disguised'.
methods.rules: When reading a Morse word as an integer, drop leading 0s. So I (00) only survives at the end of a sentence (postpositive I), and ME (110) goes first. Words starting with E, I, S, H, U, V, F, A, R, L, W, J or P cannot be expressed as distinctive numbers. FOUR to EIGHT start with dits, so Penn calls them 'not distinctive'. UE (Eugene) has a leading dit and is therefore disguised as FV/VF or via BM 2-13 = UE 21-3. In the 340 passage at #229 'the leading zero has been omitted' (ME 43 instead of ME RY).

methods.claims: Penn claims the Zodiac's sentence grammar (ME first, I last) follows from this rule, and that the father's code UE had to be hidden as FV.

methods.name: Trailing zero = 'times two' (and Morse E)
methods.summary: Appending a 0 doubles a binary number without changing its 'spelling', so a trailing zero is read as 'x2', 'II' (successor) or a final Morse E.
methods.rules: N x 2^k = N's bits + k zeros. A trailing 0 is read as 'x2' or Roman 'II' (BM II = BM's successor). A number too large for a clock face may be halved and given a multiplier (331 TIMES 2 = 662 = KING). Because Morse E = 0, 'X TIMES 2' can also supply a final E (MIK.TIMES2 = MIKE). Half a vocabulary number conveys 'one half' (see half-device). Variant ('Half' device (half a vocabulary number)): A number that is half of a vocabulary number conveys 'one half', or half of a parent's genes. Check whether a value x 2 is a vocabulary number (BER/2 = 65, GENE/2 = 50, 232/2 = 116). Example: 1:16 call -> 116 = 232 / 2 ('The Honolulu Letter had told only half the story.') Example: Date 6-5 -> 65 = half of 130 (BM 211 is about halfway between BM 159 and BM 195.)

methods.name: Power-of-two progressions and scaling
methods.summary: Positions, angles or counts that are a vocabulary number times a power of two are read as that word, and gaps in a 2^n series are read as missing members.
methods.rules: Multiplying or dividing by 2^n only shifts the binary point, so N x 2^k 'is' N. Look for series like 58 x 2^-1, 2^1, 2^2 or 2^8, 2^10 and read the absent term. Belli-letter angles may be scaled by powers of two (316 = 79 x 2^2).

methods.name: Binary expansion of a constant parsed as Morse
methods.summary: Write a mathematical constant or fraction in base two and cut its bits into Morse letters, forward or backward.
methods.rules: Expand the constant's fraction (or the whole value) in base two to n places and redivide into Morse letters or names. Penn also notes the 'curiosity' that sqrt(b) and 1/sqrt(b) share digits only in base b, so finding 1/sqrt(10) in binary 'implies' writing sqrt(10) in binary. methods.name: Arabic numerals spliced into the bit string as binary
methods.summary: Digits that appear inside a text are converted to plain base two (not Morse numerals) and spliced into the Morse bit string, so a word plus a number can spell another word.
methods.rules: A group of Arabic digits (separated from other digits by punctuation) becomes one binary number: 2 -> 10, 13 -> 1101, 17 -> 10001. Letters become Morse. The mixed string is then redivided. The Morse digit table on Penn's chart is reference only. A group of numerals counts one character per digit when measuring grid distances.

methods.name: Zodiac sentence grammar (subject + number, verb understood)
methods.summary: Penn reads hidden strings as two-part sentences: a subject (ME, I, Z, a name code) and a predicate number or word, with 'is/am' understood.
methods.rules: No verbs: the copula is omitted 'as in the modern Slavic languages'. ME (110) is prepositive; I (00) is postpositive because leading zeros vanish. NINE, the letter I (9) or two rings may stand for I. S (000) can act as 'is' ('s). The crossed circle may stand for I (ego). Examples: ME 43, I (am) 130, BM (am) I, OH (is) NINE, Z (is) OH, ID (is) 38.

methods.summary: Reverse the order of a Morse bit string (or of its units) and redivide it.

methods.name: Letter containment (a Morse letter 'contains' a shorter one)
methods.summary: Because some Morse letters are prefixes of others (I = 00 contains E = 0; G = 110 contains ME), one letter may stand in for another, and a word may be 'completed' by any letter ending in the right bit.

methods.name: Hidden redivision search (target inside a run of text)
methods.summary: Search the digitized text for any run of consecutive letters whose Morse bits contain a target word's bits. Penn treats such a run as a hidden occurrence of the word.
methods.rules: Digitize every text: letters to Morse, numerals to binary, everything else dropped. A run x 'is' a redivision of target y if y's bits lie inside x's bits, starting inside x's first letter and ending inside its last. Partial letters at both ends are allowed. It is 'perfect' if no digits are left over. Penn searched with Microsoft Word find, and converted a digital position to a literal one by dividing by 2.58 (the average Morse length of an English letter). Rarer (longer) targets count for more.

methods.name: Rule-bending redivision (ZODIAC = GENEBERTA)

timeline.event: Late 1980: Penn's father Hugh Penn tells him the Zodiac used 'radian' in a suppressed July 1970 letter. On 26 Dec 1980 Penn lays a radian on the Mt. Diablo map (Blue Rock Springs - Mt. Diablo - Presidio Heights). Within days he presents a theory to Napa Sheriff Capt. Ken Narlow.

By January Penn has his 0/1 'digital transcription' of the 340 (nine-multiples class) and reads its opening 13 bits as the pi fraction = ERAHO. From January to May he mails anonymous postcards to O'Hare (the 'Rumplestiltskin Effect'), signing one with the pseudonym MIKE REVNEC, a Morse redivision of GARETH PENN.

May-July: a New West draft and the 'Zodiac Chrestomathy' go to the FBI. The FBI Lab (26 Jun 1981) notes 'Wizard' and 'Binary Morse' substitutions but finds the bulk 'speculation'. Penn adds a calendar analysis (24 Jun) and a telephone-number analysis (30 Jun). In November, as 'George Oakes' in California magazine, he publishes the radian, Morse-to-binary and the 390:18 = 130 pi proportion. Laube's Times-Herald profile quotes 'binary Morse ... and vice versa'.

November: 'Portrait of the Artist as a Mass Murderer', California magazine (formerly New West), pp.111-114, 166-170, as 'George Oakes' and rewritten by Tom Bates. It sets out the radian on Mt. Diablo, Morse-to-binary, the 390:18 pi proportion, WIZARD with 27-sum nulls (SLAVES -> HOZH), PHOMPHIT = H2O = MT/2PI, 4-TEEN, 'cid' = DCI = XEMIT, 144114 = 38 and the Tenniel source of the 1974 figures. On p.166 Penn cites Galileo's and Huygens's discoveries 'originally published as anagrams' (priority anagrams), alongside Jeremiah's atbash and Humphries's acrostic.

Penn's series in The Ecphorizer (San Francisco Regional Mensa), 59 items from #2 (Oct 1981) to #62 (Jan 1987). The Zodiac pieces include '11.0010010000 11111101101' (#4, Dec 1981: radian, Z of postmarks, TREES = 320), 'Te Moriarty Salutamus' (#15: 340 binary, i-dot mm), 'Incline Village Unit 6' (#24: 1623 = MIKE O, permit timetable), 'One Zero Zero' (#29: crossed circle = 100, 13-cipher = MIKE O), 'The Pond of Kabbalah' and 'Sympathetic Magic at Goose Pond' (#36-37: 7120 ~ GOOSE, 4226 = BASIN), 'Thirty-Eight' (#41), 'Hide and Seek' (#46: the Grail Castle protocol), 'The Once and Future Killing' (#52: Bus Bomb geometry), 'Mike West' (#53: calls and Penn's own coded mailings), 'The Red King's Dream' (#56: chess on the call grid, 943 -> 349) and 'My Rosetta Stone' (#57: the 32-cipher). Wordplay pieces include 'More I-????-Its' (#8), 'Bumpersticker Bridge Goes Bananas' (#31: card-suit rebuses) and 'Creative Reading' (#50: reversed trademarks). Pen names in the series: Garfield Shaeffer, and '110011001010' (= G PENN).

Penn builds the Zodiac Identification Kit (ZIK) and sends a 119-page packet to the FBI. The Lab (Jan 1983) calls the results 'forced and inconsistent'. He extends the theory to the Joan Webster disappearance in Boston (Nov 1981), using map angles at benchmarks.

'Times 17' talk at a Mensa regional gathering in Santa Rosa (May): GENEBERTA redivided as ZODIAC, and his claim that O'Hare's Social Security number gives Riverside's longitude. From June Penn mails encoded stimuli (Miami Card, New York Letter) and starts reading one-ring hang-up calls as replies.

The 'telephone literature' peaks. Penn tabulates calls in calendar grids (the 'Ten-Week Message', sum 38,838), plays clock-face hide-and-seek on the USGS Concord quadrangle, and has an X printed by the Lynn Item (28 Nov 1984). He sends the Honolulu Letter (two 35-cent stamps = BM x 2).

Mensa Bulletin 'The Calculus of Evil' (Jul/Aug) gives A=1..Z=26 plus Morse 'convergence' (FRY/MERY -> ME 43), THREE = BUS = 'I am 130', 390:18 pi, the nine-multiples 340 key, and i-dot millimetre geometry (76/38 = TWO).
